_comment: The map's base layers and tile-retry policy, shared by the app and the public map island.
WHY THIS IS JSON AND NOT TYPESCRIPT (task 353):
The app's map is a Vue component in a bundle; the public map (PRD 011 §8) is a ~200-line vanilla
island on a page that deliberately loads no bundle. Both must draw the same layers — the
maintainer's instruction on 2026-09-21 — and until now the island had a fourth, different WMS
copied by hand, so the public map showed a base map nobody in the app had ever seen.
So the definitions live in a plain file that both sides can read: src/config/map.ts imports it at
build time, and publicmap.js fetches it at runtime. No code generation, no parsing of TypeScript,
and no second copy to keep in step. The island falls back to the default layer if this file cannot
be fetched, so a missing asset costs the layer switcher rather than the map.
The service paths and WMS layer names were verified against live GetCapabilities + GetMap responses
on 2026-08-24 — do NOT infer them by analogy: dtk_25_DAF answers to DTK25/dtk25/dtk_25, but
dtk_50_DAF rejects DTK50 and only accepts dtk_50. See PRD 002 §11.
FORMAT IS PER LAYER, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS LARGE. Measured against the live service (256 px tiles,
central Zealand, 2026-08-26): orto_foraar is ~137 kB/tile as PNG and ~9-14 kB/tile as JPEG, ~15x.
PNG stores photographic detail losslessly, which is exactly the wrong trade for aerial imagery on
rural mobile data — and tiles are the largest cached dataset in PRD 009's offline budget. The
topographic layers stay PNG deliberately: they are line art and text, where JPEG's block artefacts
smear thin contours and place names.
No key inside 'layers' may be anything but a layer: both sides map over its entries.

_comment: Leaflet has no built-in retry: one failed image request leaves that tile grey until the user pans
away and back. On patchy rural mobile data that is the normal case, not the exception.
Backoff is baseDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1) plus up to jitterMs, so a whole screen of failed tiles does
not retry in lockstep and hammer the service.
